- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative or low (≤0.3), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect market caution.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the following 3–5 periods.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of declining prices), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast slope in subsequent periods.
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show volatility or sentiment swings, model tends to overfit recent trends; smooth forecast by averaging last 7–10 days.
- When sentiment history includes multiple 0.00 values (indicating strong bearish sentiment), model often fails to correct downward; apply a hard floor at 10–15% below recent low if sentiment persists.
